target_vertical: Distributors, light manufacturers (assembly/process), multi-channel online retailers, food & beverage, medical/pharma, electronic components — all on QuickBooks
pricing_model: Per-named-user subscription with bundled packages (Starter/Pro/Enterprise) and optional add-on modules (mobile WMS, EDI, landed cost, manufacturing, web store, shipping workstation). Annual or monthly billing; additional users priced per seat. One-time implementation/onboarding fee on top.
starting_price_usd: Entry tier ~$79/user/month (Inventory Management); Distribution ~$99/user/month; Manufacturing ~$149/user/month per third-party listings. Vendor often quotes ~$3,000/user/year for typical configurations.
free_trial_or_freemium: No public free trial / no freemium tier — demo by appointment with sales only
shopify_supported: Native (first-party Acctivate app on Shopify App Store, built by Alterity, Inc.)
shopify_install_count: 0 public reviews; install count not disclosed on the listing
shopify_sync_direction: Bi-directional but asymmetric per entity: Shopify -> Acctivate for orders, customers, B2B companies, custom order fields. Acctivate -> Shopify for inventory availability and shipment/tracking notifications.
shopify_synced_entities: Sales orders (import), customers (import, including Shopify B2B Companies mapped to Acctivate customers/contacts), custom sales-order fields (mapped to Acctivate standard or custom fields), product Available quantity (export, for items flagged 'Available on web'), shipments and tracking numbers (export, which then trigger Shopify shipment notifications to the buyer). Product/variant master data is generally not pushed from Acctivate to Shopify — products are typically managed in Shopify and matched into Acctivate by SKU.
shopify_service_item_support: [uncertain] — Acctivate has service/non-stock item types internally, but documentation of explicit non-physical/service line sync from Shopify is not clearly published
shopify_multi_store_support: Yes — multiple web stores (including multiple Shopify stores) per Acctivate company are supported via separate web store templates
shopify_pos_support: [uncertain] — no dedicated Shopify POS module documented; POS transactions would flow only if they appear in the Shopify Orders API
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: Partial — Acctivate supports importing Shopify B2B orders where the Shopify Company is mapped to an Acctivate customer and the purchaser becomes a contact on the sales order. Native sync of Shopify B2B price lists / catalogs / company locations as first-class objects is not documented.
shopify_markets_support: [uncertain] — no Acctivate documentation explicitly addressing Shopify Markets multi-market pricing, duties, or landed-cost fields
shopify_metafield_to_erp_field_mapping: Partial — custom sales-order fields defined in Shopify can be mapped to standard or custom fields in Acctivate. Generic product-metafield mapping is not explicitly documented.
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants are matched to Acctivate products by SKU; option/variant titles flow through on the order. Master variant creation in Shopify from Acctivate is not the primary direction.
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Scheduled polling — sync runs on a configurable interval (5, 15, 30, or 60 minutes) or on demand. Not webhook-driven real-time.
shopify_known_limitations: Polling-based sync (minimum 5-minute interval) rather than real-time webhooks; reviewers note limited out-of-the-box reporting, weak audit trail, and a learning curve. Product master data is typically managed in Shopify, not pushed from Acctivate. The Shopify App Store listing has no reviews. Service-item / Shopify POS / Shopify Markets behavior is not clearly documented.
etsy_native_or_third_party: Not available natively — only possible via a third-party middleware that exposes XML/CSV order feeds, or via Acctivate's published XML schema for custom developer integration
etsy_order_import: Not applicable (would require custom XML integration or middleware)
etsy_known_limitations: Etsy is not on Acctivate's list of supported web store platforms; users would have to route Etsy through ShipStation, a 3rd-party middleware, or build a custom integration against Acctivate's XML schema
amazon_supported: Third-party / indirect — Amazon is not a directly supported Acctivate channel; recommended path is to connect Amazon Seller Central to ShipStation (Professional plan) and then import orders from ShipStation into Acctivate
amazon_marketplaces: Whatever ShipStation supports (US, CA, MX, UK, EU, AU, etc.) — Acctivate itself does not enumerate marketplaces
amazon_seller_types: FBM is the primary supported model via ShipStation. FBA orders can also be downloaded via ShipStation; Vendor Central is not addressed.
amazon_synced_entities: Orders, customers, shipments/tracking — all relayed through ShipStation. Listings, inventory, settlements, returns, and Amazon customer messaging are not synced by Acctivate.
amazon_listing_creation: Not supported — Acctivate cannot create or update Amazon listings
amazon_buy_shipping: Not supported directly (no in-app Amazon Buy Shipping)
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: Not supported as a native workflow — Acctivate has no FBA inbound shipment plan creation
amazon_sp_api_inbound_v2024_03_20: Not applicable — Acctivate does not integrate directly with SP-API
amazon_settlement_report_handling: Not handled by Acctivate — settlements and Amazon fee reconciliation are not features; users post these in QuickBooks separately or via a tool like A2X
amazon_marketplace_facilitator_tax_handl: Not specifically handled by Acctivate; tax journaling for marketplace-facilitator transactions has to be configured in QuickBooks
amazon_multi_account_support: Effectively yes (multiple ShipStation channels can feed one Acctivate company), but not native to Acctivate
amazon_known_limitations: No direct SP-API integration; everything routes through ShipStation, meaning no FBA inbound, no settlement reconciliation, no repricer, no Buy Shipping, no listing management, no Amazon messaging
xero_supported: None (Xero is not an Acctivate-supported accounting backend)
xero_known_limitations: Acctivate is QuickBooks-only; no Xero integration exists
qb_online_supported: Yes — QuickBooks Online is supported as a primary accounting backend
qb_desktop_supported: Yes — QuickBooks Desktop (Pro, Premier, Enterprise) is the original and still primary backend, integrated via Intuit's SDK / QuickBooks integration components
qb_app_certified: Listed on the Intuit App Store / QuickBooks App Marketplace; Acctivate is a long-standing Intuit Solution Provider partner
qb_synced_entities: Customers (bi-directional), vendors (bi-directional), Chart of Accounts (QuickBooks -> Acctivate), Payment Methods (QuickBooks -> Acctivate), payment terms and customer types (bi-directional), sales reps / employees (QB -> Acctivate), finalized customer invoices and credit memos (Acctivate -> QB), vendor bills and credits (Acctivate -> QB), customer payments and receipts, inventory adjustments posted as summary GL entries (Acctivate -> QB). Sales orders and purchase orders stay in Acctivate and are NOT pushed to QuickBooks. Product master, inventory quantities, and individual inventory transactions stay in Acctivate.
qb_accounting_sync_mode: invoice_per_order — Acctivate posts finalized invoices and bills 1:1 to QuickBooks. Inventory movement is posted as summarized GL adjustments to keep QuickBooks asset/COGS accounts in balance.
qb_cogs_journal_method: perpetual_per_movement (with landed cost roll-in) — Acctivate maintains perpetual inventory using Average, FIFO, LIFO, Standard, or Actual costing per product, and posts COGS to QuickBooks per shipment/invoice. Landed cost is rolled into inventory value before COGS recognition.
qb_multi_currency: Yes — multi-currency AR/AP postings supported in line with QuickBooks' multi-currency feature
qb_class_location_mapping: Yes — QuickBooks Class can be mapped on transactions; QBO Location mapping is supported in newer releases. Acctivate v15 added QuickBooks Automated Sales Tax integration.
qb_known_limitations: Once integrated, Acctivate owns inventory and does not sync product master, quantities, or per-movement inventory transactions to QuickBooks — only summary journal entries. Sales orders and POs live only in Acctivate. Some sync errors require the new v15 Sync Log Window for visibility. QBO sync uses the official QBO REST API but is run on schedule, not real-time.
other_ecom_channels: WooCommerce (native), BigCommerce (V2 native), Magento / Adobe Commerce (V1 + V2 native), eBay (native), Shift4Shop (native), Volusion (native), ChannelAdvisor (native, opens TikTok / Walmart / etc. indirectly), AspDotNetStorefront, CoreCommerce, SparkPay, ZNode, custom XML file import. No native TikTok Shop, Wix, Squarespace, Faire, Square, or Walmart direct.
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Yes — Acctivate supports Kits (assembled at time of sale) and Assemblies (made-to-stock); selling a kit/assembly decrements component quantities automatically and BOMs can be multi-level
other_accounting_integrations: None — Acctivate's value proposition is being QuickBooks-only. No Sage, Xero, NetSuite, Zoho Books, MYOB, FreshBooks, or Wave integration.
bom_support: Yes — full Bill of Materials module included in the Manufacturing edition
production_orders: Yes — Assemblies (make-to-stock) and Custom/Process Assemblies (make-to-order, with WIP tracking and yield variance for process/batch manufacturing such as food, beverage, nutraceutical). Routings/operations exist but are lighter than a true MES.
batch_lot_tracking: Yes — unlimited lot numbers with expiration date, lot reference, lot specification; full traceability from receipt through production to fulfillment
serial_tracking: Yes — unlimited serial number tracking through receipt, production, and shipment
bin_location_support: Yes — Multiple Location module supports aisle, rack, shelf, bin, truck, or any user-defined sub-location below the warehouse
multi_warehouse: Yes — unlimited warehouses; transfers between warehouses supported
barcoding: Yes — barcode label generation and printing; Acctivate Mobile WMS (Android, formerly Windows Mobile) supports scan-driven receiving, picking, transfers, counts, and assembly
purchase_orders: Yes — POs with partial receipts, drop-ship POs, special-order POs, reorder-point automation, supplier price lists, vendor-specific SKUs and pricing
supplier_management: Yes — vendor records with multiple ship-from addresses, lead times, MOQs, vendor product numbers, vendor pricing, and vendor history
landed_cost_support: Yes — dedicated Landed Cost module that allocates freight, duty, insurance and broker fees across received PO lines (by weight, value, quantity, or manually); supports landed cost from the same vendor as the PO or a separate vendor
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: Single base currency for inventory valuation; foreign-currency PO costs are converted at receipt. Multi-currency applies to AR/AP rather than per-currency on-hand valuation.
ai_demand_forecasting: No — traditional reorder-point and min/max replenishment only; no ML-driven forecasting documented as of v15
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Rule-based reorder suggestions (reorder point / min-max / sales velocity) — not AI/ML
public_api: No public REST/GraphQL API for general developer use. Acctivate's documented integration path is its native XML schema for web store integrations and Crystal Reports / ODBC access into the underlying SQL Server database for reporting. Customers requiring deep integration typically work directly against the SQL Server back end.
webhook_event_coverage: No outbound webhooks. Acctivate consumes inbound APIs (Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, eBay, ShipStation, QuickBooks) on a polling schedule.
integration_architecture: Native first-party connectors (Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, eBay, Shift4Shop, Volusion, ChannelAdvisor, ShipStation, StarShip, EDI via SPS Commerce/TrueCommerce, QuickBooks). No iPaaS dependency. Custom integrations done via published XML schema or direct SQL.
zapier_make_support: No native Zapier / Make / n8n connector
mobile_app: Acctivate Mobile WMS — Android app for rugged warehouse devices (formerly Windows Mobile). Functions: receiving, picking, packing, inventory counts, transfers, location moves, assemblies, lookup. No general-purpose customer/sales mobile app.
mobile_barcode_scanning_app: Yes — Acctivate Mobile WMS is barcode-scanner driven (rugged Android devices with integrated scanners recommended)
sync_frequency: QuickBooks: on-demand or scheduled (manual trigger most common in Desktop, scheduled in QBO). Web stores (Shopify/WooCommerce/BigCommerce/Magento/eBay): configurable polling at 5, 15, 30, or 60 minute intervals, or manual. ShipStation: scheduled polling. EDI: scheduled. None real-time / webhook driven.
shipping_carrier_integrations: FedEx, UPS, USPS, DHL — both directly and via StarShip and ShipStation. International carriers via ShipStation.
shipping_label_buying: Yes — via the optional Shipping Workstation license integrating with StarShip or ShipStation for label printing and rate shopping
three_pl_integrations: EDI-based 3PL integration via SPS Commerce / TrueCommerce (940 warehouse shipping orders, 945 shipment confirmations). No native ShipBob / ShipHero / Extensiv connector.
edi_support: Yes — full EDI module with native integration to SPS Commerce and TrueCommerce; supports 850/855/856/810/940/945 and other common transactions for retail trading partners (Home Depot, Walmart, Amazon Vendor, etc.)
g2_rating: [uncertain] — G2 lists Acctivate with feature-level scores (Product Direction 7.5, Quality of Support 8.0, Ease of Setup 7.1) but the aggregate star rating was not clearly visible in search results
notable_customers: [uncertain] — vendor publishes industry case studies (electronic components, truck parts, nutraceutical, food & beverage distributors) but does not headline named logos publicly
last_major_release: Acctivate Version 15 (2025) — added Customer/Vendor autocomplete, dedicated Edit Customer Ship-To window, improved Customer Price Rules, QuickBooks Automated Sales Tax integration, edit Sales Invoice header without voiding, and a Sync Log Window for visibility of sync errors
owner_parent_company: Alterity, Inc. (creators of Acctivate) was acquired by CAI Software, LLC in August 2023
last_funding_event: Acquisition by CAI Software, LLC — August 2023 (terms undisclosed)
public_status_page_uptime: [uncertain] — no public status page found (Acctivate is primarily an on-premise / customer-hosted SQL Server application, so uptime is customer-managed; QuickBooks Online sync depends on Intuit's uptime)
